newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - B.Midland makes $1 bln Airbus order.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - B.Midland makes $1 bln Airbus order.

text.p: Privately-owned airline British Midland said on Wednesday it had ordered 20 aircraft from Airbus Industrie worth $1 billion.
This was the biggest order placed by a British company with the European aircraft consortium.

Sir Michael Bishop, chairman of British Midland, said the deal was also significant because it was the first time the airline had broken away from its traditional supplier Boeing Co of the United States.

British Midland, which operates domestic and European routes, has signed a memorandum of understanding to order eight Airbus A321 planes seating 196 passengers and 12 A320s which seat 160. A full deal will be signed later.
Bishop told Reuters in an interview that the decision to use Airbus did not signal the end of its relationship with Boeing.
"We decided on a policy of having both Airbus and Boeing. We are not dropping Boeing and we will be adding more Boeing aircraft in future," said Bishop.

That could be through leasing deals or buying second hand aircraft. "In the past we've been almost exclusively customers of Boeing. But for technical and financial reasons we went for Airbus. The Airbus A321 was suited to our short haul routes and the financial terms were more favourable," he said.
Airbus spokesman David Voskuhl said: "This is the largest single deal we have done with the UK and British Midland is a new customer." Other British customers include British Airways and Virgin.

The Airbus consortium is owned by Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale of France and Daimler-Benz Aerospace -- a unit of Daimler Benz AG of Germany, which both own 37.9 percent, plus British Aerospace which holds 20 percent and Spain's Construcciones Aeronauticas SA with 4.2 percent.
One part of the aircraft deal still to be decided is who wins the engine order.

On one side stands CFMI, a Franco-American consortium which includes General Electric Co. On the other is the IAE partnership which includes Britain's Rolls Royce Plc, Pratt & Whitney of the United States and the Japanese Aero Engine Consortium.
Bishop said the decision on engines would be made by July.
